topic: Burt Reynolds: dramatic, emotionally charged rise, fall, and redemption
notes:
Dramatic/emotional framing, not a career-recap listicle. Research facts with sources:
- Peak: #1 box office star 5 straight years, 1978-1982 (Britannica/Variety). Deliverance (1972) was the breakthrough; Smokey and the Bandit (1977, with Sally Field) grossed $100M+.
- Earned $4-5M per film at his peak (Variety).
- Self-destruction: invested in a restaurant chain that cost him up to $30M (Celebrity Net Worth); in 1990 borrowed $4M from CBS against Evening Shade syndication that never came, leaving him $3.7M in debt to the network.
- Dec 1996: Chapter 11 bankruptcy. $6.65M in assets vs $11.2M in liabilities. Creditors included the IRS, Chase, CAA, William Morris, and his own toupee maker ($121,000 owed) - Celebrity Net Worth.
- 1993 divorce from Loni Anderson: ~$250k/month in payments during proceedings, eventually a $2M settlement plus a vacation home; drove his net worth down toward $5M (Men's Journal/Celebrity Net Worth).
- Auctioned his own Hollywood memorabilia in 2014 (Julien's Auctions) to fend off financial trouble - including a horse-and-rider sculpture from his Jupiter, FL theatre and the stagecoach from his wedding to Anderson.
- Personal regret: called Sally Field 'the one that got away' in his 2015 memoir 'But Enough About Me,' saying 'I was just an arrogant jerk' (Fox News/Hollywood Reporter).
- Redemption beat: turned down Boogie Nights seven times, was talked into it by PT Anderson, earned a Best Supporting Actor Oscar nomination (1998).
- Death: heart attack, Sept 6 2018, age 82, in a Florida hospital; his niece said it was unexpected despite a long health decline that included a quintuple bypass in 2010; described as gaunt, under 100 lbs, unable to walk unassisted near the end (Nicki Swift/Variety).
Angle: rise (Deliverance/Bandit/#1 star) -> self-inflicted collapse (restaurants, CBS debt, bankruptcy, brutal divorce) -> the regret (Sally Field) -> the redemption swing (Boogie Nights) -> the quiet, physically diminished end. Sources: britannica.com, variety.com, celebritynetworth.com, mensjournal.com, foxnews.com, hollywoodreporter.com, nickiswift.com, news.artnet.com.
